# Qyl.Telemetry.Tests

The four primary projects are `Qyl.Telemetry.Tests` (shared support), `Qyl.Telemetry.UnitTests`, `Qyl.Telemetry.IntegrationTests`, and `Qyl.Telemetry.EndToEndTests`. `Qyl.Telemetry.Tests.slnx` contains exactly those four entries. Capture and application/probe projects remain build dependencies; do not add them as extra primary solution entries. Contract parity and Collector consumer cases belong to IntegrationTests/Contracts. Build with `./build.sh` (Fallout Check); pins live in `Version.props` and `global.json`. The build defaults to two logical processors and one MSBuild worker, preserving an explicitly supplied processor limit.

Keep exactly three `testconfig.json` files, beside the UnitTests, IntegrationTests and EndToEndTests `.csproj` files; pin `$schema` to the MSTest version in `global.json`.
Configure terminal output through `commandLineOptions`: UnitTests uses `failed` results, `Failed` stdout/stderr and `off` progress/ANSI; IntegrationTests/EndToEndTests use `all`, `All` and `auto`; set `mstest.output.captureTrace` to `Result` for UnitTests and `Live` for IntegrationTests/EndToEndTests.

## General test defaults

Unless a component-specific test policy applies:
- Name tests `<Method>_<Scenario>_<Expected>`.
- Mark unit tests with `[TestCategory("Unit")]`.
- Seal concrete test classes.

Read the nearest `AGENTS.md` and project skill before editing. A component-specific policy overrides these defaults only within that component. Keep MSTest at the version pinned by `global.json` (currently 4.5.1); package versions belong in `Directory.Packages.props`, not individual project files. Preserve the native Microsoft.Testing.Platform runner and the NativeAOT requirements in `SKILL.md`.

## Repository test execution

The source checkout must sit inside the parent qyl checkout: contract integration tests reference its Collector and contracts projects. CI recreates that layout and restores the MCP Bun dependencies; set the repository variable `QYL_SOURCE_REF` to pin the matching parent commit.

Run the unit suite without restoring with `pwsh ./eng/test.ps1 -Suite Unit -NoRestore`.
The script is the supported test entry point; do not substitute a direct `dotnet test` command. `Qyl.Telemetry.Tests.slnx` defines the repository's build and test graph. The `Unit` suite selects `TestCategory=Fast`, as required by its component policy, uses the native MTP runner, emits TRX results, and preserves the test exit code. Restore dependencies first when using `-NoRestore`. Other selections are `-Suite Integration`, `-Suite EndToEnd`, and `-Suite All`; the build gate calls the same script. Respect the caller's processor limit; the script defaults to two processors and one test module at a time.

## Inspection and completion

Run InspectCode against the **entire `Qyl.Telemetry.Tests.slnx`** before making changes and again after the requested work. Bash is supported. On the development Mac, run:

```bash
PATH="/usr/local/share/dotnet:$PATH" jb inspectcode Qyl.Telemetry.Tests.slnx --output=inspectcode.sarif
```

Use the installed .NET host and equivalent paths on a remote worker. The repository's `InspectCode` gate uses this same canonical solution; `eng/inspection.slnx` mirrors its four primary projects. Every agent working in this repository follows this rule, regardless of its starting project. Inspect and fix findings across all four primary project areas (shared support, unit, integration and end-to-end), and any other project registered in the solution; do not restrict repairs to the project that originally prompted the task.

Fix findings at their cause without asking for confirmation for routine in-scope repairs. When a production-code fix requires a test adjustment, make both changes and run the regression test that proves the production behavior. Do not weaken assertions, hide diagnostics, skip tests, or claim completion from compilation alone. Finish only after the relevant tests prove the fix and the final inspection succeeds; explain a concrete external blocker if that cannot be achieved. Keep intermediate messages to progress and blockers, and save the final report for completion.

## Binding rules for every test

[SKILL.md](SKILL.md): assertions by their exact semantics (AreEqual, HasCount, AreSequenceEqual with SequenceOrder.InAnyOrder, IsEmpty, ContainsSingle, ThrowsExactly), NativeAOT first with the native MTP runner, VSTest forbidden, AreEquivalent and Assert.That(Expression) off limits in NativeAOT code, nothing weakened. Verified against MSTest 4.5.1 on 2026-10-22; version-specific guidance rechecked on 2026-10-23.

[SKILL.md](SKILL.md), section "Test-code rules": the name is the specification (`<Method>_<Scenario>_<Expected>`, unless a component-specific policy overrides it, no comments), one behavior per test with the MSTest assertion API, DataRow discriminators as constants, no try/catch/finally inside a test, time through TimeProvider, the gate decides. Read it before writing or reviewing a test.

## Skill per project

| Project | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| Qyl.Telemetry.Tests/Qyl.Telemetry.Tests.csproj | [Support skill](Qyl.Telemetry.Tests/skills/qyl-telemetry-support/SKILL.md) |
| Qyl.Telemetry.UnitTests/Qyl.Telemetry.UnitTests.csproj | [Unit skill](Qyl.Telemetry.UnitTests/skills/qyl-telemetry-unit/SKILL.md) |
| Qyl.Telemetry.IntegrationTests/Qyl.Telemetry.IntegrationTests.csproj | [Integration skill](Qyl.Telemetry.IntegrationTests/skills/qyl-telemetry-integration/SKILL.md) |
| Qyl.Telemetry.EndToEndTests/Qyl.Telemetry.EndToEndTests.csproj | [End-to-end skill](Qyl.Telemetry.EndToEndTests/skills/qyl-telemetry-end-to-end/SKILL.md) |

Support references: [api.md](Qyl.Telemetry.Tests/skills/qyl-telemetry-support/references/api.md) (APIs and sources) and [telemetry-policies.md](Qyl.Telemetry.Tests/skills/qyl-telemetry-support/references/telemetry-policies.md) (the policy attributes).

# Unit tests

Inherit [repository guidance](../AGENTS.md) and the [binding test skill](../SKILL.md). Read the [project skill](skills/qyl-telemetry-unit/SKILL.md) before changing this component.

Use deterministic in-memory dependencies and FakeTimeProvider. Unit tests do not start network listeners, processes or real Collectors.

## Component-specific test policy

This policy overrides the root test defaults for this project:
- Name tests `Should_<ExpectedBehavior>_When_<Condition>`.
- Mark tests with `[TestCategory("Fast")]`.
- Do not seal test classes; derived fixtures must remain possible.

Run `pwsh ./eng/test.ps1 -Suite Unit -NoRestore` from the repository root after dependencies have been restored. The script maps the Unit suite to the Fast category. Keep the same test behavior and data-row counts when changing names or metadata.

README.md.text:
`Qyl.Telemetry.Tests` provides shared test support. `Qyl.Telemetry.UnitTests`, `Qyl.Telemetry.IntegrationTests`, and `Qyl.Telemetry.EndToEndTests` cover the three test scopes described in [src/AGENTS.md](src/AGENTS.md). New tests use MSTest 4.5.1. Package versions belong in `Directory.Packages.props`, not individual project files.

The repository build and test entry point is `Qyl.Telemetry.Tests.slnx`, containing exactly those four primary projects. Run tests through `pwsh ./eng/test.ps1`; the default unit selection uses the component-specific `Fast` category. Full build, coverage and inspection run through `./build.sh`.

Shared product and runtime pins are imported from the parent qyl `Version.props`; this repository keeps only its test-specific pins. Contracts, CLI and orchestration use project references. SemanticConventions also uses the local source checkout when present, with the shared package pin as the fallback. `Qyl.Telemetry.Hosting` remains a package dependency because its source is not in this checkout.

Rider's ReSharper Build can remain enabled. Real IDE builds explicitly build local project references before resolving their assemblies, preserving the selected Debug or Release configuration and building their transitive dependencies. Design-time builds do not run this step. The solution still contains only the four primary projects.

Projects with `UsesQylCollector=true` build the parent Collector and stage its output under `qyl/collector` beside the tests. They do not download a published Collector package, so local contract and Collector changes are exercised together on the next build.

evals/qyl-investigate/README.md.text:
# qyl-investigate eval

Replays the reviewer prompts of the qyl connector submission through Claude Code against
the live server and scores what came back: which tools were chosen, whether the answer
names the seeded findings, and what it cost. Run it before and after one change to the
qyl-investigate skill or to the server's instructions to see what the change did.

## What it needs

- `claude` (Claude Code CLI) signed in, and the qyl MCP server signed in as the reviewer
  under the server name `qyl` (`claude mcp list` shows `qyl: https://mcp.qyl.at/mcp - Connected`).
  The replay passes only that server (`--strict-mcp-config`), so the sign-in stored for the
  name `qyl` decides which project answers. The reviewer sign-in reaches `review`, the
  project reseeded daily at 00:00 UTC with the answer-key incidents (releases are named by the
  UTC date, and from qyl 17.0.9 by the date and the 12-hour slot: checkout YYYY.MM.DD[.HH].1 is the
  bad release and .2 the fix, regional .3 fails in eu) and
  fed healthy traffic every 10 minutes; the plugin's own server
  entry (`plugin:qyl:qyl`) is the owner's project and is not used.
- The installed qyl plugin (`claude plugin list` shows `qyl@ancplua-anthropic`), or a plugin
  directory passed with `--plugin-dir`. The replay loads the plugin with `--plugin-dir` and
  drops user-scope settings (`--setting-sources project`), so exactly one copy of the
  qyl-investigate skill is under test.
- Python 3.

## Run

```sh
python3 -I eng/evals/replay.py                       # the four read prompts, 3 runs each, sonnet
python3 -I eng/evals/replay.py --judge               # plus an LLM grade of each answer against its rubric (haiku)
python3 -I eng/evals/replay.py --case what-changed --runs 1 --model opus
python3 -I eng/evals/replay.py --tag writes          # the save-query case; it deletes what it saved
python3 -I eng/evals/replay.py --dry-run             # print the claude commands only
python3 -I eng/evals/replay.py --no-plugin --tag read --tag writes --model opus --judge   # the reviewer's view: no plugin, server instructions and tool descriptions only
```

Results land in `results/<timestamp>-<label>/`: the raw stream and the parsed run per case
and run, `summary.json` and `summary.md`. The results directory is not committed.

## Measure one changed line

```sh
python3 -I eng/evals/replay.py --label baseline
python3 -I eng/evals/replay.py --variant evals/qyl-investigate/variants/example-one-line.json
python3 -I eng/evals/compare.py evals/qyl-investigate/results/<baseline dir> evals/qyl-investigate/results/<variant dir>
```

A variant spec names a file in the plugin and the exact line to replace; the replay copies
the plugin, applies the replacement (it must match once) and loads the copy. `compare.py`
prints B minus A per case: score, tool calls, turns, tokens, cost and seconds.

## Scores

| Score | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| tools | share of the case's expected steps satisfied; each step lists the tools that satisfy it. 0 when a forbidden tool was called (the read prompts forbid every write tool) or an argument check failed (what-changed requires a 24 hour window). |
| mentions | share of the case's `must_mention` patterns found in the final answer: the findings, not ids or counts, because the project is reseeded with fresh ids every day. |
| judge | with `--judge`: a 0..1 grade of the final answer against the case's rubric by a second model. |
| score | mean of the components that ran. |

`verify_fix` may answer `pending` right after a reseed and `passed` once healthy traffic has
accumulated; the checkout case accepts the verdict as returned and the rubric asks for that.

## Binding the tool names

`tool-names.json` is the only place that knows the server's tool and argument names. Cases
use the logical names on its left side. After the coordinator's "tools final" (the T2 merge
renames and merges tools), update the right side and `bound_to`; the cases stay as they are.

# Test scopes, native composition and build metadata

Inherit the [repository guidance](../AGENTS.md). This directory is the scope index; the existing compiled projects remain at their current paths. Choose the observable boundary before selecting a fixture. A project is a compiled code boundary; a skill describes a task or review goal. Do not invent competing MSTest skills just because several test projects exist.

| Scope | Project and governing skill |
| --- | --- |
| Unit | [Qyl.Telemetry.UnitTests](../Qyl.Telemetry.UnitTests/AGENTS.md), [unit skill](../Qyl.Telemetry.UnitTests/skills/qyl-telemetry-unit/SKILL.md) |
| Integration | [Qyl.Telemetry.IntegrationTests](../Qyl.Telemetry.IntegrationTests/AGENTS.md), [integration skill](../Qyl.Telemetry.IntegrationTests/skills/qyl-telemetry-integration/SKILL.md) |
| End-to-end | [Qyl.Telemetry.EndToEndTests](../Qyl.Telemetry.EndToEndTests/AGENTS.md), [end-to-end skill](../Qyl.Telemetry.EndToEndTests/skills/qyl-telemetry-end-to-end/SKILL.md) |
| Shared test helpers | [Qyl.Telemetry.Tests](../Qyl.Telemetry.Tests/AGENTS.md), [support skill](../Qyl.Telemetry.Tests/skills/qyl-telemetry-support/SKILL.md); [NativeAOT capture](../Qyl.Telemetry.Tests.Capture/AGENTS.md) |

All scopes share the [native runner and assertion semantics](../SKILL.md). Build metadata belongs in the project files, `Directory.Packages.props`, `global.json`, and `Qyl.Telemetry.Tests.slnx`; do not replace project references with copied binaries.
